summary: OpenAI released gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b, two open-weight mixture-of-expert reasoning models with agentic tool-use capabilities, publishing weights, inference implementations, tool environments and tokenizers under an Apache 2.0 license.

mechanisms.reason: The models are described as using an efficient mixture-of-expert architecture explicitly aimed at reducing inference cost, though no concrete figures are given.
mechanisms.quote: We present gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b, two open-weight reasoning models that push the frontier of accuracy and inference cost.

practices.reason: Released open-weight reasoning models with stated agentic tool-use capability and permissive licensing enable self-hosting and fine-tuning for production agentic pipelines.
practices.quote: We optimize the models to have strong agentic capabilities (deep research browsing, python tool use, and support for developer-provided functions), all while using a rendered chat format that enables clear instruction following and role delineation.

practices.reason: The paper cites benchmark performance across math, coding and safety but gives no specifics an engineer could directly reuse as an eval instrument.
practices.quote: Both models achieve strong results on benchmarks ranging from mathematics, coding, and safety.

practices.reason: The mixture-of-expert architecture and distillation/RL training pipeline described could be examined as a template for lowering serving cost on self-hosted deployments.
practices.quote: The models use an efficient mixture-of-expert transformer architecture and are trained using large-scale distillation and reinforcement learning.

practices.reason: Release of weights alongside inference implementations, tool environments and tokenizers changes what a team must integrate to self-host these models.
practices.quote: We release the model weights, inference implementations, tool environments, and tokenizers under an Apache 2.0 license to enable broad use and further research.

notable_reason: A frontier lab releasing open-weight reasoning models with agentic tool-use under a permissive license is a significant self-hosting option for engineering teams.
